Plot survey responses as a serpentine of stacked bars

Source: R/survey_sequence.R
survey_sequence.Rd

A survey sequence shows the distribution of responses to a set of rating items as one 100% stacked bar per item. The bars are the bands of a serpentine joined by U-turns, so a long instrument fits in one panel in its item order and the share of each response level can be compared between items. Heiberger and Robbins (2014) discuss the design of stacked bar charts for rating scales.

survey_sequence() accepts raw responses or a table of counts. Segments are colored by response level, with a diverging palette by default, and carry their percentage when wide enough. Items can be sorted by mean or by net agreement. Each U-turn takes the color midway between the levels at the two ends it joins, or a neutral grey.

sequential_dist() draws the same display with a single-hue palette for scales without a neutral midpoint. survey_snake() shows each response as a tick and can show correlations between adjacent items.

Usage

survey_sequence(
  counts,
  labels = NULL,
  levels = NULL,
  band_height = 28,
  band_gap = 14,
  plot_width = 500,
  colors = NULL,
  show_percent = TRUE,
  min_segment = 34,
  arc_style = c("gradient", "neutral"),
  arc_opacity = 0.5,
  sort_by = c("none", "mean", "net"),
  shadow = TRUE,
  show_legend = TRUE,
  label_color = "#333333",
  label_size = 0.85,
  label_align = "left",
  reverse_rtl = FALSE,
  start_from = c("left", "right"),
  flow = c("snake", "natural"),
  title = NULL,
  margin = c(top = 30, right = 10, bottom = 55, left = 100),
  background = "white"
)

Arguments

counts

Responses: a data frame of raw responses (one row per respondent, one column per item), a numeric matrix of counts (items in rows, response levels in columns), or a data frame of counts. A data frame is read as raw responses when its columns hold few distinct whole-number or categorical values relative to its number of rows.

labels

Item labels, one per item. NULL (default) uses the row names of a count table, or, for raw responses, the column names with the number of responses.

levels

Response levels in scale order. NULL (default) uses the column names of a count table, or, for raw responses, the factor levels or the sorted distinct values. For raw responses the levels must match the values in the data.

band_height

Height of each band in plot units (default 28).

band_gap

Gap between bands in plot units (default 14).

plot_width

Length of each band in plot units (default 500).

colors

One color per response level, in scale order. Only the first length(levels) colors are used, so pass snake_palette(name, n = <number of levels>). NULL (default) uses a red-to-blue diverging palette.

show_percent

Print percentages inside the segments (default TRUE).

min_segment

Minimum segment width, in plot units, for a percentage to be printed (default 34).

arc_style

"gradient" (default) colors each U-turn midway between the levels at its two ends; "neutral" draws it grey.

arc_opacity

Opacity of the U-turns, between 0 and 1 (default 0.5).

sort_by

Order of the items: "none" (default, input order), "mean" (increasing item mean) or "net" (increasing share of responses above the middle level minus share below; the mean for scales with fewer than four levels).

shadow

Draw drop shadows (default TRUE).

show_legend

Draw the legend (default TRUE).

label_color, label_size

Color and size multiplier of the item labels (defaults "#333333" and 0.85).

label_align

Alignment of the item labels: "left" (default), "right", or "direction" to follow each band's reading direction.

reverse_rtl

Reverse the order of levels on bands that read right to left, so every band starts with the lowest level in its reading direction (default FALSE: lowest level on the left of every band).

start_from

Side on which the first band starts: "left" (default) or "right".

flow

"snake" (default): bands alternate direction. "natural": every band reads in the same direction.

title

Plot title, or NULL (default) for none.

margin

Named numeric vector of top, right, bottom and left margins in plot units (default c(top = 30, right = 10, bottom = 55, left = 100)).

background

Background color (default "white").

Value

The plot is drawn on the current device. The function returns, invisibly, an object of class snake_layout: a list describing the drawn geometry, with bands (a data frame with one row per item band giving its index, position, and drawing and reading direction), arcs (a list with one element per U-turn), canvas and plot_area (dimensions in plot units), orientation, flow and params (the sizes used).

References

Heiberger, R. M., & Robbins, N. B. (2014). Design of diverging stacked bar charts for Likert scales and other applications. Journal of Statistical Software, 57(5), 1-32. doi:10.18637/jss.v057.i05

See also

sequential_dist() for single-hue bars; survey_snake() for individual responses and item correlations; snake_palette() for level colors.

Examples

# Ten emotion items, sorted by net score
survey_sequence(ema_emotions, sort_by = "net")


# Study motivation items with another diverging palette
motivation <- subset(student_survey,
                     select = Mot_Disappointed:Mot_Enjoyment)
survey_sequence(motivation, sort_by = "mean",
                colors = snake_palette("ocean", n = 5))
